T|__EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT__
C|**CASTELLAN TECHNOLOGIES, INC.**
P|This Employment Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of [July 14, 2025] (the "Effective Date"), by and between **Castellan Technologies, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), and **Priya Venkataraman** ("Employee").
P|**WHEREAS**, the Company and Employee are parties to that certain offer letter dated June 9, 2025, executed by the Company on June 9, 2025 and accepted by Employee on June 12, 2025 (the "Offer Letter"), which contemplates that the Company and Employee will enter into this Agreement on or prior to the Start Date (as defined below);
P|**WHEREAS**, the Company desires to employ Employee in the position of Senior Vice President, Engineering, on the terms and conditions set forth herein, and Employee desires to accept such employment on such terms and conditions; and
P|**WHEREAS**, the parties intend that this Agreement memorialize and implement the terms of the Offer Letter, define the terms "Cause," "Good Reason," and "Change of Control" as contemplated by the Offer Letter, and, upon its effectiveness, supersede and replace the Offer Letter and any other prior offer letter, term sheet, or other agreement or representation regarding Employee'"'"'s employment with the Company, including without limitation any oral or written representations made during the recruitment or interview process;
P|**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:
H|1. Employment and Duties
P|**1.1 Position and Title.** The Company hereby employs Employee in the position of Senior Vice President, Engineering, reporting directly to the Company'"'"'s Chief Executive Officer (the "CEO"). Employee shall perform such duties and responsibilities as are customarily associated with such position and as may be assigned from time to time by the CEO or the Board of Directors of the Company (the "Board"). Subject to Employee'"'"'s rights under Section 7 upon a resignation for Good Reason, Employee'"'"'s duties, title, and reporting relationships may be modified from time to time in the Company'"'"'s discretion, consistent with Employee'"'"'s experience and qualifications.
P|**1.2 Principal Place of Employment.** Employee'"'"'s principal place of employment shall be the Company'"'"'s headquarters located at 1900 Technology Parkway, Suite 400, San Jose, California 95134. Under the Company'"'"'s hybrid work arrangement, Employee'"'"'s position requires in-office presence at least three (3) days per week. The Company reserves the right to modify Employee'"'"'s work schedule and hybrid work requirements upon reasonable notice, subject to applicable law and Employee'"'"'s rights under Section 7 upon a resignation for Good Reason.
P|**1.3 Exclusive Service; Outside Activities.** During the term of Employee'"'"'s employment, Employee shall devote Employee'"'"'s full business time, attention, skill, and best efforts to the performance of Employee'"'"'s duties hereunder. Employee shall not engage in any other business activity, whether or not such activity is pursued for gain, profit, or other pecuniary advantage, without the prior written consent of the CEO; *provided, however*, that Employee may (a) serve on civic or charitable boards or committees, (b) deliver lectures or fulfill speaking engagements, and (c) manage personal investments, in each case so long as such activities do not individually or in the aggregate materially interfere with the performance of Employee'"'"'s duties hereunder or create a conflict of interest with the Company'"'"'s business. Service on the board of directors (or similar governing body) of any for-profit entity shall require the prior written consent of the CEO. Nothing in this Section 1.3 restricts Employee'"'"'s lawful conduct occurring during nonworking hours away from the Company'"'"'s premises to the extent protected by California Labor Code Section 96(k) or other applicable law.
P|**1.4 Start Date.** Employee'"'"'s employment under this Agreement shall commence on July 14, 2025 (the "Start Date").
P|**1.5 Exempt Status.** Employee'"'"'s position is a full-time position classified as exempt from overtime requirements under the Fair Labor Standards Act and applicable California law.
P|**1.6 Conditions of Employment.** Consistent with the Offer Letter, Employee'"'"'s employment is contingent upon (a) satisfactory completion of a background check, conducted in compliance with the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act, the California Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act, the California Fair Chance Act (Cal. Gov. Code § 12952), and other applicable law; (b) Employee'"'"'s execution of this Agreement, including the CIIPR Agreement attached as Exhibit A and the Arbitration Agreement attached as Exhibit C; and (c) Employee'"'"'s provision, within three (3) business days following the Start Date, of documentation establishing Employee'"'"'s identity and authorization to work in the United States as required by law (Form I-9).
H|2. At-Will Employment
P|**2.1 At-Will Status.** Employee'"'"'s employment with the Company is "at-will." Either the Company or Employee may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without Cause (as defined below), and with or without advance notice, subject to the provisions of this Agreement, including the severance provisions of Section 7. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as creating an implied or express contract of employment for any definite term. The at-will nature of Employee'"'"'s employment may be modified only by a written agreement expressly so providing that is approved by the Board and signed by Employee and the CEO.
P|**2.2 Notice of Resignation.** Employee agrees to provide the Company with no less than thirty (30) days'"'"' prior written notice of Employee'"'"'s voluntary resignation (the "Notice Period"), other than a resignation for Good Reason, which shall be governed by the notice and cure provisions of Section 7.2(c). During the Notice Period, Employee shall continue to perform Employee'"'"'s duties and cooperate fully with the Company to ensure an orderly transition of Employee'"'"'s responsibilities. The Company may, in its sole discretion, waive all or any portion of the Notice Period and accelerate Employee'"'"'s separation date, in which case Employee shall receive Base Salary through the accelerated separation date, and such acceleration shall not constitute a termination of employment by the Company without Cause or give rise to Good Reason.
P|**2.3 Termination by the Company.** The Company may terminate Employee'"'"'s employment at any time, with or without Cause, subject to the severance provisions of Section 7 of this Agreement.
H|3. Compensation
P|**3.1 Base Salary.** The Company shall pay Employee an initial annualized base salary of $485,000 (the "Base Salary"), payable in accordance with the Company'"'"'s standard payroll practices, less applicable withholdings and deductions. Employee'"'"'s Base Salary shall be paid semi-monthly (twenty-four (24) pay periods per year) in equal installments. The Base Salary shall be subject to review by the Board or its Compensation Committee (the "Compensation Committee") on an annual basis, and may be adjusted in the Board'"'"'s sole discretion; *provided, however*, that the Base Salary shall not be reduced below the initial rate set forth herein (or, if higher, the then-current rate) without Employee'"'"'s prior written consent.
P|**3.2 Signing Bonus.** The Company shall pay Employee a one-time signing bonus in the amount of $150,000 (the "Signing Bonus"), payable within thirty (30) days following the Start Date, subject to applicable withholdings and deductions. Employee must be actively employed by the Company on the date the Signing Bonus is paid in order to receive the Signing Bonus. The Signing Bonus is intended to assist with Employee'"'"'s transition to the Company and to recognize the compensation Employee is forgoing by joining the Company, and it is not subject to repayment.
P|**3.3 Annual Performance Bonus.** Employee shall be eligible to participate in the Company'"'"'s annual performance bonus program and to earn an annual performance bonus (the "Annual Bonus") with a target amount equal to forty percent (40%) of Employee'"'"'s Base Salary (the "Target Bonus") and a maximum payout opportunity equal to sixty percent (60%) of Employee'"'"'s Base Salary. Based on the initial Base Salary, the Target Bonus is $194,000 and the maximum Annual Bonus is $291,000. The actual amount of the Annual Bonus, if any, is discretionary and shall be determined by the Board or the Compensation Committee, in consultation with the CEO, based on the achievement of individual and Company performance criteria established by the Board or the Compensation Committee for the applicable performance period. The Annual Bonus for a calendar year shall be payable in the first calendar quarter of the following calendar year, and in all events no later than March 15 of such following calendar year. Employee must be actively employed by the Company on the date the Annual Bonus is paid in order to earn and receive the Annual Bonus; no partial or pro-rated bonus shall be payable upon termination of employment prior to the payment date except as expressly provided in Section 7 of this Agreement. For calendar year 2025, the Annual Bonus shall be pro-rated based on the number of days Employee is employed during such calendar year divided by 365.
H|4. Equity Awards
P|**4.1 Stock Option Grant.** Subject to the approval of the Board or the Compensation Committee, Employee shall be granted an option to purchase 60,000 shares of the Company'"'"'s common stock (the "Option") pursuant to the Company'"'"'s 2021 Equity Incentive Plan (as amended from time to time, the "Plan") and the terms and conditions of a stock option agreement to be entered into between the Company and Employee (the "Option Agreement"). The Company shall recommend the grant of the Option at the first regularly scheduled meeting (or action by written consent) of the Board or the Compensation Committee following the Start Date. The Option shall have an exercise price per share equal to the fair market value of a share of the Company'"'"'s common stock on the date of grant, as determined by the Board in good faith in accordance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code"). The Option shall be an incentive stock option to the maximum extent permitted under Section 422 of the Code (including the $100,000 annual limitation of Section 422(d) of the Code), and the remainder, if any, shall be a nonstatutory stock option. The "Vesting Commencement Date" shall be August 1, 2025. The Option shall vest as follows: twenty-five percent (25%) of the shares subject to the Option (15,000 shares) shall vest on the first anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date, and one forty-eighth (1/48th) of the shares subject to the Option (1,250 shares) shall vest on each monthly anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date thereafter, such that the Option shall be fully vested on the fourth anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date, in each case subject to Employee'"'"'s continued service with the Company through each such vesting date. No portion of the Option shall vest prior to the first anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date. The Option shall be subject to all other terms and conditions of the Plan and the Option Agreement.
P|**4.2 Restricted Stock Unit Grant.** Subject to the approval of the Board or the Compensation Committee, Employee shall be granted 120,000 restricted stock units (the "RSU Award") pursuant to the Plan and the terms and conditions of an RSU award agreement to be entered into between the Company and Employee (the "RSU Agreement"), to be recommended for grant at the same time as the Option. The RSU Award shall vest as follows: twenty-five percent (25%) of the RSUs (30,000 RSUs) shall vest on the first anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date, and the remaining seventy-five percent (75%) of the RSUs shall vest in twelve (12) equal quarterly installments of 7,500 RSUs on each three-month anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date thereafter, such that the RSU Award shall be fully vested on the fourth anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date, in each case subject to Employee'"'"'s continued service with the Company through each such vesting date. The RSU Award shall be settled in shares of the Company'"'"'s common stock as soon as practicable (and in no event later than thirty (30) days) following each applicable vesting date, in accordance with Section 409A of the Code. The RSU Award shall be subject to all other terms and conditions of the Plan and the RSU Agreement.
P|**4.3 Change of Control Acceleration.** If, during the Change of Control Period, Employee experiences a Qualifying Termination (each as defined in Section 7.8), then, subject to Section 7.5, fifty percent (50%) of the then-unvested portion of each of Employee'"'"'s then-outstanding equity awards (including the Option and the RSU Award) shall immediately vest and, as applicable, become exercisable, effective as of the date the Release (as defined in Section 7.5) becomes effective and irrevocable. In order to give effect to this Section 4.3, (a) any unvested portion of Employee'"'"'s equity awards shall remain outstanding (but shall not vest, other than pursuant to this Section 4.3) following a Qualifying Termination until the earlier of the date the Release becomes effective and irrevocable and the Release Deadline, and (b) if the Release does not become effective and irrevocable by the Release Deadline, such unvested portion shall be forfeited without consideration. [Unless otherwise provided in the applicable award agreement, any performance-based vesting conditions shall be deemed achieved at target for purposes of this Section 4.3.] Any RSUs that vest pursuant to this Section 4.3 shall be settled within thirty (30) days following the date the Release becomes effective and irrevocable, subject to Section 7.6. The acceleration provisions of this Section 4.3 shall apply to all equity awards held by Employee and shall be reflected in each applicable award agreement.
P|**4.4 General Equity Terms.** All equity awards described in this Section 4 shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the Plan and the applicable award agreements. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the Plan or award agreements, the Plan shall govern, except with respect to the vesting schedules set forth in Sections 4.1 and 4.2 and the acceleration provisions set forth in Section 4.3, which shall control. Employee acknowledges that the Company makes no representations regarding the tax treatment of any equity award, and Employee agrees to consult with Employee'"'"'s own tax advisor regarding such matters.
H|5. Benefits
P|**5.1 Health and Welfare Benefits.** Employee shall be entitled to participate in such health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, and other employee benefit plans and programs as the Company may maintain from time to time for its senior executives, subject to the eligibility requirements and other terms and conditions of such plans and programs. As of the Effective Date, such plans include the Castellan Wellness Plus Plan (the Company'"'"'s group health plan), in which Employee shall be eligible to enroll effective as of the Start Date; enrollment information will be provided during onboarding by Greystone Benefits Administration, Inc., the Company'"'"'s third-party benefits administrator. The Company reserves the right to modify, amend, or terminate any benefit plan or program at any time in its sole discretion, in accordance with applicable law and the terms of such plans and programs.
P|**5.2 Retirement Benefits.** Employee shall be eligible to participate in the Company'"'"'s 401(k) retirement savings plan, subject to the terms and conditions of such plan. The Company currently matches fifty percent (50%) of Employee'"'"'s elective deferral contributions up to six percent (6%) of Employee'"'"'s Base Salary, subject to applicable Internal Revenue Service limits (including the annual compensation limit under Section 401(a)(17) of the Code and the elective deferral limit under Section 402(g) of the Code) and the terms of the plan as may be amended from time to time.
P|**5.3 Life Insurance.** Employee shall be eligible for coverage under the Company'"'"'s group life insurance program, as may be in effect from time to time, and, as of the Effective Date, for a supplemental life insurance benefit of $500,000 under the Company'"'"'s Executive Life Program, subject to the terms, conditions, and any underwriting requirements of the applicable policy. Specific coverage amounts and terms are governed by the applicable plan documents and policies. The Company reserves the right to modify or discontinue such coverage at any time, in accordance with applicable law and the terms of such plans.
P|**5.4 Paid Time Off.** Employee shall be eligible to take paid time off in accordance with the Company'"'"'s flexible time off policy as in effect from time to time. The flexible time off policy provides Employee with the discretion to take time off as needed, without a fixed accrual balance, subject to reasonable advance scheduling consistent with business needs and the terms of such policy as communicated to employees. Because no paid time off accrues under the flexible time off policy, no paid time off will be paid out upon termination of employment; *provided* that any vested, unused vacation or paid time off that may have accrued under any prior or other Company policy shall be paid as required by California Labor Code Section 227.3. Employee shall also be entitled to paid sick leave in accordance with, and in no event less than that required by, the California Healthy Workplaces, Healthy Families Act and any applicable local ordinance.
P|**5.5 Business Expenses.** The Company shall reimburse Employee for all reasonable and necessary business expenses incurred in the performance of Employee'"'"'s duties, in accordance with California Labor Code Section 2802 and subject to the Company'"'"'s expense reimbursement policies in effect from time to time. Employee shall submit expense reports with supporting documentation in accordance with Company policy. All reimbursements shall be made no later than the last day of the calendar year following the calendar year in which the expense was incurred, in accordance with Section 409A of the Code.
H|6. Garden Leave During Notice Period
P|At any time during the Notice Period described in Section 2.2 (or during any notice period provided by the Company to Employee in connection with a termination of Employee'"'"'s employment by the Company), the Company may, in its sole discretion, require Employee to remain away from the Company'"'"'s offices and refrain from performing any duties or contacting any employees, customers, clients, or business partners of the Company on Company business for all or any part of such notice period (the "Garden Leave Period"). In no event shall the Garden Leave Period extend beyond the effective date of termination of Employee'"'"'s employment.
P|During the Garden Leave Period, Employee shall remain an employee of the Company and shall continue to receive Employee'"'"'s Base Salary and benefits, and shall continue to vest in Employee'"'"'s equity awards, in accordance with the Company'"'"'s standard payroll practices, benefit plan terms, and the applicable award agreements. Employee shall remain bound by all obligations under this Agreement and the CIIPR Agreement (as defined below) during the Garden Leave Period, including Employee'"'"'s duty of loyalty to the Company. Employee shall remain available to provide transitional assistance and respond to inquiries from the Company during the Garden Leave Period, and shall make Employee reasonably available during normal business hours for such purposes. During the Garden Leave Period, Employee shall not commence employment with, or provide services (whether paid or unpaid) to, any other person or entity without the prior written consent of the Company. The Company may, in its sole discretion, elect to shorten the Garden Leave Period at any time by providing written notice to Employee. Placement of Employee on garden leave in accordance with this Section 6 shall not, by itself, constitute Good Reason. Nothing in this Section 6 restricts Employee'"'"'s activities following the termination of Employee'"'"'s employment.

H|7. Termination and Severance
P|**7.1 Termination for Cause.** The Company may terminate Employee'"'"'s employment for Cause at any time, effective immediately upon written notice to Employee (or such later date as specified in such notice). For purposes of this Agreement, "Cause" shall mean the occurrence of any of the following:
I|(a) Employee'"'"'s material breach of this Agreement, the CIIPR Agreement, or any other agreement between Employee and the Company, which breach, if curable, is not cured within fifteen (15) days after written notice thereof from the Company;
I|(b) Employee'"'"'s conviction of, or plea of guilty or *nolo contendere* to, a felony or any crime involving moral turpitude, fraud, dishonesty, or embezzlement;
I|(c) Employee'"'"'s willful misconduct or gross negligence in the performance of Employee'"'"'s duties hereunder, which is materially injurious to the Company;
I|(d) Employee'"'"'s material violation of any written Company policy, including but not limited to policies regarding workplace conduct, information security, anti-harassment, and anti-discrimination;
I|(e) Employee'"'"'s continued failure to substantially perform Employee'"'"'s duties hereunder (other than as a result of physical or mental disability) after written notice specifying the deficiency and a thirty (30) day opportunity to cure; or
I|(f) Employee'"'"'s commission of any act of fraud, misappropriation, or dishonesty against the Company.
P|Upon any termination of Employee'"'"'s employment for any reason, Employee shall be entitled to receive: (i) accrued but unpaid Base Salary through the date of termination; (ii) reimbursement for any unreimbursed business expenses properly incurred prior to the date of termination in accordance with Section 5.5; (iii) any vested, unused vacation or paid time off required to be paid under applicable law; and (iv) any vested benefits required to be provided under applicable law or under the terms of any employee benefit plan in which Employee participates (collectively, the "Accrued Obligations"). Amounts described in clauses (i) through (iii) shall be paid within the time required by California Labor Code Sections 201 through 203. In the event of a termination for Cause, Employee shall be entitled to receive only the Accrued Obligations. For the avoidance of doubt, Employee shall not be entitled to any severance, bonus, or equity vesting following a termination for Cause.
P|**7.2 Termination Without Cause or Resignation for Good Reason Outside the Change of Control Period.** If Employee experiences a Qualifying Termination at any time other than during the Change of Control Period, then, subject to Section 7.5, Employee shall be entitled to the Accrued Obligations and, in addition, the Company shall provide Employee with:
I|(a) continued payment of Employee'"'"'s Base Salary, at the rate in effect immediately prior to the date of termination, for a period of nine (9) months following the date of termination (the "Severance Period"; $363,750 in the aggregate at the initial Base Salary), payable in accordance with the Company'"'"'s regular payroll practices, less applicable withholdings and deductions, commencing as provided in Section 7.5; and
I|(b) the COBRA benefits described in Section 7.4 for up to nine (9) months following the date of termination.
P|**7.3 Termination Without Cause or Resignation for Good Reason During the Change of Control Period.** If Employee experiences a Qualifying Termination during the Change of Control Period, then, in lieu of (and not in addition to) the payments and benefits described in Section 7.2, and subject to Section 7.5, Employee shall be entitled to the Accrued Obligations and, in addition, the Company shall provide Employee with:
I|(a) continued payment of Employee'"'"'s Base Salary, at the rate in effect immediately prior to the date of termination (or, if greater, immediately prior to the Change of Control), for a period of twelve (12) months following the date of termination ($485,000 in the aggregate at the initial Base Salary), payable in accordance with the Company'"'"'s regular payroll practices, less applicable withholdings and deductions, commencing as provided in Section 7.5;
I|(b) a lump-sum cash payment equal to one hundred percent (100%) of Employee'"'"'s Target Bonus for the calendar year in which the date of termination occurs ($194,000 at the initial Target Bonus), less applicable withholdings and deductions, payable on the first regular payroll date following the date the Release becomes effective and irrevocable (subject to the second-year rule in Section 7.5) and in all events no later than March 15 of the calendar year following the calendar year in which the date of termination occurs;
I|(c) the COBRA benefits described in Section 7.4 for up to twelve (12) months following the date of termination; and
I|(d) the equity acceleration described in Section 4.3.
P|The total cash severance payable under Sections 7.3(a) and 7.3(b) (excluding COBRA benefits) is $679,000 at the initial Base Salary and Target Bonus. If Employee'"'"'s Qualifying Termination occurs after the date on which Employee commenced receiving payments under Section 7.2 and it is subsequently determined that such Qualifying Termination occurred during the Change of Control Period, any amounts paid under Section 7.2 shall offset the amounts payable under this Section 7.3, and the remaining amounts payable under Section 7.3 shall be paid in the same form and on the same schedule as the payments under Section 7.2 to the extent required to comply with Section 409A of the Code.
P|**7.4 COBRA Benefits.** If Employee timely and properly elects continuation coverage under the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985, as amended, or any state law of similar effect ("COBRA"), the Company shall reimburse Employee for the COBRA premiums paid by Employee for coverage for Employee [and Employee'"'"'s eligible dependents who were covered under the Company'"'"'s group health plan on the date of termination] (the "COBRA Benefits") until the earliest of (a) the end of the applicable period set forth in Section 7.2(b) or 7.3(c), (b) the date Employee becomes eligible for group health coverage through a subsequent employer (and Employee shall promptly notify the Company of such eligibility), and (c) the date Employee ceases to be eligible for COBRA continuation coverage. Reimbursements shall be made monthly within thirty (30) days following Employee'"'"'s submission of proof of payment, subject to Section 7.5. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Company determines in its sole discretion that it cannot provide the COBRA Benefits without potentially violating, or incurring an excise tax or penalty under, applicable law (including Section 2716 of the Public Health Service Act or Section 105(h) of the Code), the Company shall in lieu thereof pay Employee a taxable monthly payment equal to the COBRA premium for such coverage for the remainder of the applicable period, which payments shall be made regardless of whether Employee elects COBRA continuation coverage.
P|**7.5 Release Requirement.** Employee'"'"'s receipt of any severance payments and benefits under Sections 4.3, 7.2, 7.3, and 7.4 (other than the Accrued Obligations) shall be conditioned upon: (a) Employee'"'"'s execution and non-revocation of a separation agreement and general release of claims in a form acceptable to the Company (the "Release"), which Release shall include a release of all claims against the Company, its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents, shall not impose any post-employment restrictive covenant that is not contained in the CIIPR Agreement, and shall comply with applicable law (including California Government Code Section 12964.5 and, if applicable, the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act); (b) Employee'"'"'s resignation from all officer and director positions with the Company and its affiliates in accordance with Section 7.9; and (c) Employee'"'"'s continued compliance in all material respects with Employee'"'"'s obligations under the CIIPR Agreement. The Release must be executed and become effective and irrevocable within sixty (60) days following the date of termination (the "Release Deadline"). Severance payments shall commence on the first regular payroll date following the date on which the Release becomes effective and irrevocable, with the first payment including any amounts that would have been paid had the Release been effective on the date of termination. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the sixty (60) day period following the date of termination spans two calendar years, severance payments (and any payment or settlement under Section 4.3 that constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation) shall not commence or be made until the first regular payroll date in the second calendar year, to the extent required to comply with Section 409A of the Code. If Employee fails to execute the Release by the Release Deadline, or if Employee revokes the Release, Employee shall not be entitled to any severance payments or benefits (other than the Accrued Obligations).
P|**7.6 Section 409A Compliance.** The parties intend that all payments and benefits under this Agreement be exempt from, or comply with, Section 409A of the Code and the Treasury Regulations and guidance thereunder ("Section 409A"), including the short-term deferral exception under Treas. Reg. § 1.409A-1(b)(4) and the separation pay exception under Treas. Reg. § 1.409A-1(b)(9)(iii), and this Agreement shall be interpreted accordingly. Any payment that is conditioned upon a termination of employment and that constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation shall be paid only upon Employee'"'"'s "separation from service" within the meaning of Section 409A. It is intended that each installment of the severance payments and benefits provided under this Agreement shall be treated as a separate "payment" for purposes of Section 409A. Neither the Company nor Employee shall have the right to accelerate or defer the delivery of any such payments or benefits except to the extent specifically permitted or required by Section 409A. If Employee is a "specified employee" within the meaning of Section 409A(a)(2)(B)(i) of the Code at the time of Employee'"'"'s separation from service, any payments or benefits that constitute nonqualified deferred compensation shall not be paid or provided until the earlier of (i) the date that is six (6) months and one (1) day following Employee'"'"'s separation from service, or (ii) the date of Employee'"'"'s death (the "Delay Period"). Upon the expiration of the Delay Period, all payments and benefits delayed pursuant to this Section 7.6 shall be paid or provided to Employee in a lump sum, without interest. To the extent any expense reimbursement or in-kind benefit is subject to Section 409A, the amount eligible for reimbursement or in-kind benefits in one calendar year shall not affect the amount eligible in any other calendar year, and the right to reimbursement or in-kind benefits is not subject to liquidation or exchange for another benefit.
P|**7.7 Resignation Without Good Reason; Death or Disability.** Employee may resign from employment at any time by providing written notice to the Company in accordance with Section 2.2. Upon a resignation by Employee other than for Good Reason, Employee shall be entitled to receive only the Accrued Obligations, and Employee shall not be entitled to any severance payments or benefits under this Agreement. Employee'"'"'s employment shall terminate automatically upon Employee'"'"'s death. The Company may terminate Employee'"'"'s employment upon Employee'"'"'s Disability. For purposes of this Agreement, "Disability" shall mean Employee'"'"'s inability to perform the essential functions of Employee'"'"'s position, with or without reasonable accommodation, for a period of ninety (90) consecutive days or one hundred twenty (120) days in any twelve (12) month period, as determined by the Board in good faith based upon competent medical evidence; *provided* that no termination for Disability shall occur during any period of job-protected leave to which Employee is entitled under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act, the California Family Rights Act, or other applicable law, and any such determination shall be made in compliance with the California Fair Employment and Housing Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Upon termination due to death or Disability, Employee (or Employee'"'"'s estate or legal representative) shall be entitled to receive the Accrued Obligations.
P|**7.8 Certain Definitions.** For purposes of this Agreement:

 ["Exh. A § A-1: confidentiality covers \"personnel information, compensation data\"; no protected-activity carve-outs", "Lab.  ["Exh. C § C-2: \"National Arbitration Council\"", "Not a recognized employment arbitration provider, and its rules cannot be identified.  ["Exh. C § C-3: arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware; Template § 11.1 allows Delaware law", "Lab. An out-of-state venue also weighs heavily in an unconscionability analysis.", "Santa Clara County, California. California law throughout (§ 11.1; § A-7).", "Low after the change."],
 ["Exh. C § C-4: arbitration costs \"shared equally\"", "Under Armendariz v. Cost-splitting is a classic substantive-unconscionability defect. Separately, Code Civ. Proc. §§ 1281.97–1281.98 impose strict deadlines for the employer to pay arbitration fees, and late payment can forfeit the right to arbitrate.", "Company pays all arbitration-unique costs (the employee'"'"'s filing fee is capped at the court filing fee).  ["Exh. C § C-6: confidentiality of proceedings", "Blanket confidentiality has been held unconscionable in California employment arbitration (e.g., Ramos v. Superior Court, 28 Cal. Uber Techs., 14 Cal. 5th 1104 (2023), allow arbitration of individual PAGA claims, but non-individual claims survive.", "Individual PAGA claims go to arbitration.  ["Exh.  ["§ 2.2: 90-day mandatory resignation notice; forfeiture of \"accrued but unpaid\" bonus for short notice", "Not in the Offer Letter, which provides at-will employment \"with or without notice.\" The forfeiture operates as a penalty. H("V. Issues in the Offer Letter Itself")
P("**1. 401(k) match is overstated.** The Offer Letter states a maximum annual Company match of $14,550 (50% × 6% × $485,000). The plan can only take into account compensation up to the Code § 401(a)(17) limit ($350,000 for 2025), which caps the match at about $10,500 (50% × 6% × $350,000). The match also requires her to defer at least 6% of covered pay ($21,000). That is within the 2025 § 402(g) deferral limit of $23,500, but 6% of her full salary ($29,100) is not. The Draft states the formula \"subject to applicable IRS limits\" and omits the dollar figure. Because the incorrect figure is in a signed document, we recommend the Company send a short written clarification (or that the Draft add an acknowledgment) to forestall a misrepresentation claim. If the plan uses a true-up or a different compensation definition, the figure may differ; confirm with the plan administrator.")
P("**2. Undefined terms that drive severance.** \"Cause,\" \"Good Reason,\" and \"Change of Control\" are used throughout but expressly left to the Employment Agreement, and the Template contained no Good Reason concept at all. The Draft'"'"'s definitions are reasonable for a Company-side first draft, but because the economic entitlements are already fixed by a signed letter, an aggressively narrow Good Reason or broad Cause definition may draw a claim that the Company is undercutting the bargained-for protection. I drafted Good Reason to track the 409A safe harbor and the triggers customary for an SVP-level executive.")
P("**3. Math reconciles.** I checked every computed figure in the Offer Letter: target bonus $194,000 (40%); maximum $291,000 (60%); 9 months'"'"' salary $363,750; CoC cash $485,000 + $194,000 = $679,000; RSUs 30,000 + (12 × 7,500) = 120,000; options 15,000 + (36 × 1,250) = 60,000. All are correct except the 401(k) figure in item 1.")
P("**4. Internal tension on at-will status.** The acceptance block states \"this offer letter is not an employment contract,\" yet the letter promises severance. Severance promises in a signed offer letter are generally enforceable regardless of such a disclaimer. The Draft resolves the tension by restating those terms in a binding agreement.")
P("**5. No pre-CoC protection window.** Double-trigger protection applies only to terminations \"within 12 months following\" a CoC. A termination in anticipation of a deal (e.g., 60–90 days before closing) receives only the non-CoC package. I did not add a look-back period, because it is not in the Offer Letter, but expect a request (Part VII).")
P("**6. Signing bonus has no clawback.** The Offer Letter does not condition the $150,000 signing bonus on retention, and the Draft does not add a repayment obligation. Adding one now would be a new, adverse term requiring her consent. It would also face California limits on \"stay-or-pay\" arrangements: wage-forfeiture and deduction rules, and newly enacted legislation (AB 692) restricting repayment obligations in employment agreements entered into on or after January 1, 2026. If the Company nonetheless wants a clawback, we should analyze it separately before raising it.")
P("**7. Equity is subject to Board approval.** The share numbers are fixed, but the exercise price will be the FMV on the grant date. Any delay in Board action after the Start Date may raise her exercise price. That is a common source of disputes, particularly if a new 409A valuation lands in the interim.")

 "**Executive Life Program.** Confirm the $500,000 benefit is insured, whether underwriting or evidence of insurability applies, and whether group-term coverage above $50,000 will produce imputed income under Code § 79.",

 "**Template remediation.** The Template'"'"'s non-compete, non-solicit, IP, arbitration, and garden-leave provisions present the same problems for every California hire. Code § 12964.5 (notice of the right to consult an attorney and at least 5 business days to consider), the OWBPA if she is 40 or older (21 days to consider, 7 days to revoke, which fits inside the 60-day Release Deadline), and Civ. Severance should be structured to fit the short-term deferral and separation pay exceptions. The separation pay exception is capped at 2× the lesser of annualized compensation or the § 401(a)(17) limit ($700,000 for 2025) and requires payment by the end of the second year after separation. The 12-month CoC salary continuation ($485,000) fits. The lump-sum target bonus ($194,000) is paid by March 15 of the following year.", "Added an exemption / compliance statement, a \"separation from service\" requirement, and reimbursement and in-kind rules. P("**1. 401(k) match is overstated.** The Offer Letter states a maximum annual Company match of $14,550 (50% × 6% × $485,000). The plan can only take into account compensation up to the Code § 401(a)(17) limit ($350,000 for 2025), which caps the match at about $10,500 (50% × 6% × $350,000). The match also requires her to defer at least 6% of covered pay ($21,000). That is within the 2025 § 402(g) deferral limit of $23,500, but 6% of her full salary ($29,100) is not. The Draft states the formula \"subject to applicable IRS limits\" and omits the dollar figure. Because the incorrect figure is in a signed document, we recommend the Company send a short written clarification (or that the Draft add an acknowledgment) to forestall a misrepresentation claim. If the plan uses a true-up or a different compensation definition, the figure may differ; confirm with the plan administrator.")
P("**2. Undefined terms that drive severance.** \"Cause,\" \"Good Reason,\" and \"Change of Control\" are used throughout but expressly left to the Employment Agreement, and the Template contained no Good Reason concept at all. The Draft'"'"'s definitions are reasonable for a Company-side first draft, but because the economic entitlements are already fixed by a signed letter, an aggressively narrow Good Reason or broad Cause definition may draw a claim that the Company is undercutting the bargained-for protection. I drafted Good Reason to track the 409A safe harbor and the triggers customary for an SVP-level executive.")
P("**3. Math reconciles.** I checked every computed figure in the Offer Letter: target bonus $194,000 (40%); maximum $291,000 (60%); 9 months'"'"' salary $363,750; CoC cash $485,000 + $194,000 = $679,000; RSUs 30,000 + (12 × 7,500) = 120,000; options 15,000 + (36 × 1,250) = 60,000. All are correct except the 401(k) figure in item 1.")
P("**4. Internal tension on at-will status.** The acceptance block states \"this offer letter is not an employment contract,\" yet the letter promises severance. Severance promises in a signed offer letter are generally enforceable regardless of such a disclaimer. The Draft resolves the tension by restating those terms in a binding agreement.")
P("**5. No pre-CoC protection window.** Double-trigger protection applies only to terminations \"within 12 months following\" a CoC. A termination in anticipation of a deal (e.g., 60–90 days before closing) receives only the non-CoC package. I did not add a look-back period, because it is not in the Offer Letter, but expect a request (Part VII).")
P("**6. Signing bonus has no clawback.** The Offer Letter does not condition the $150,000 signing bonus on retention, and the Draft does not add a repayment obligation. Adding one now would be a new, adverse term requiring her consent. It would also face California limits on \"stay-or-pay\" arrangements: wage-forfeiture and deduction rules, and newly enacted legislation (AB 692) restricting repayment obligations in employment agreements entered into on or after January 1, 2026. If the Company nonetheless wants a clawback, we should analyze it separately before raising it.")
P("**7. Equity is subject to Board approval.** The share numbers are fixed, but the exercise price will be the FMV on the grant date. Any delay in Board action after the Start Date may raise her exercise price. That is a common source of disputes, particularly if a new 409A valuation lands in the interim.")

**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** \[Supervising Partner\]

**FROM:** \[Associate\]

**DATE:** \[●\]

**CLIENT:** Castellan Technologies, Inc. (the "Company")

**RE:** Draft Employment Agreement for Priya Venkataraman (Senior Vice President, Engineering) -- Conforming Changes, Legal Issues, and Open Items

**[\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_]{.underline}**\_

**[I. Summary]{.underline}**

You asked me to prepare an employment agreement for Priya Venkataraman using the Company's form Employment Agreement (the "Template") and her executed offer letter dated June 9, 2025 (countersigned June 12, 2025) (the "Offer Letter"), and to flag changes, issues, and open items. The draft is delivered as **employment-agreement-draft.docx** (the "Draft"). The Draft (1) conforms every economic and structural term to the Offer Letter, (2) supplies the definitions of "Cause," "Good Reason," and "Change of Control" that the Offer Letter expressly deferred to the Employment Agreement, and (3) removes or revises Template provisions that are unenforceable, or affirmatively unlawful, for a California-based employee. Bracketed text in the Draft marks items requiring client confirmation. The most significant points are:

> • **The Template materially under-delivers on the signed Offer Letter.** It provides 6 months of salary continuation only on a without-Cause termination, no COBRA, no Good Reason protection, no change of control severance, and a placeholder for equity acceleration. The Offer Letter commits to 9 months' salary and COBRA on a without-Cause or Good Reason termination, and an enhanced 12-month package (12 months' salary, a lump-sum target bonus, 12 months' COBRA, and 50% double-trigger equity acceleration) within 12 months after a Change of Control. Using the Template as-is would breach the Offer Letter and the supersession clause would purport to extinguish those rights. All have been conformed (Draft §§ 4.3, 7.2--7.5, 7.8).
>
> • **The Template's equity terms are wrong.** It references a "2017 Stock Option Plan" (the Offer Letter grants under the **2021 Equity Incentive Plan**, and RSUs cannot be granted under a stock option plan) and provides monthly 1/48th vesting with no cliff for both awards. The Offer Letter provides a one-year cliff for both awards, then monthly vesting for the Option and quarterly vesting for the RSUs. Corrected (Draft §§ 4.1, 4.2).
>
> • **Several Template provisions are unlawful or unenforceable in California and create affirmative liability**, most importantly the 12-month nationwide post-employment non-compete (void under Bus. & Prof. Code § 16600; including it is itself unlawful under § 16600.5 and exposes the Company to a private action and attorneys' fees), the post-employment employee and customer non-solicits, an invention assignment without the Labor Code § 2870 carve-out and notice, a 6-month post-termination garden leave, and an arbitration agreement that designates an unrecognized provider ("National Arbitration C5239
